output_list.reason: The 'transfer' function has an overflow bug. When 'value' is zero, the check balances[msg.sender] = safeSub(balances[msg.sender], _value); will not execute, allowing a malicious attacker to overflow the totalSupply of a user's balance, aka 'rate control' attack.

The 'transferFrom' function has an overflow bug. When 'value' is zero, the check allowed[_from][msg.sender] = safeSub(_allowance, _value); will not execute, allowing a malicious attacker to overflow the _allowance of an user, aka 'rate control' attack.

The 'setApproval' function has an overflow bug. When '_addedValue' is zero, the check if ((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)) throw; will not execute, allowing a malicious attacker to set arbitrary 'allowance' of an user, aka 'rate control' attack.

The 'subApproval' function has an overflow bug. When '_subtractedValue' is zero, the check if (_subtractedValue > oldVal) { allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = 0; } will not execute, allowing a malicious attacker to set arbitrary 'allowance' of an user, aka 'rate control' attack.

The 'setUpgradeMaster' function has a vulnerability related to access control. It allows anyone to set the 'upgradeMaster' address, which can be exploited to make the master inaccessible, aka 'wrong logic' attack.
